chunks: And Abu al-Abbas al-Baqqaq narrated, he said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

about a man who bought a female slave, freed her, then married her, and did not observe her waiting period (istibra') to ensure she was not pregnant. He said: 'It was permissible for him to do so, and if he did not do so, there is no harm.' And the captive woman is also observed for waiting (istibra') by one menstruation.

key_terms.اِسْتَبْرَأْ: observed waiting period (to confirm pregnancy status)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man frees a slave girl and marries her without waiting to see if she is pregnant?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a man who emancipates a female slave and subsequently marries her is not required to observe the full waiting period (*istibra'*) for pregnancy confirmation, rendering the marriage valid even if omitted. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the *istibra'* of freed slaves (*mukattabah* or *umm walad*) compared to other categories, emphasizing that the primary purpose of lineage verification is satisfied. The mention of a single menstruation for captives further illustrates the distinct legal status of *sabiyah* in marital contexts.
